name: Borvo
text: Borvo is a god honoured across Gaul as the guardian of healing springs. He also carried the names Bormanus and Bormo in some lands. The Romans of the period recognised him as none other than Apollo. At Vichy in France a carving shows Borvo seated in armour. A shield and helmet rest at hand, and a horned serpent coils upwards toward him. His usual companion is Damona, yet the form called Bormanus takes Bormana for a mate instead. Veneration of Borvo and Damona together marked the healing waters at Bourbonne-les-Bains in France. Some old traditions name Sirona or Dirona as a possible mother for him. He is bound as well to the spring goddesses Sul and the Suleviae in the company of scholars. His name carries the sense of to boil, which suits a god who rules over hot, bubbling waters.

okr.objective: Describe Borvo, the Gaulish god of the healing springs, with his cult sites and companions.
key_results: Borvo is a Gaulish god of the healing springs.
At Vichy he was carved seated in armour with a horned serpent rising towards him.
He had Damona as his usual consort, with Bormana for Bormanus.
He was worshipped with Damona at Bourbonne-les-Bains in France.
He may have been the son of Sirona or Dirona, and the Romans equated him with Apollo.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
